reason: atip restores SIGPIPE at start (app::restore_sigpipe); atip_check_54 closes the reader before the write and was shown to fail without the fix
summary: Standards pass: atip exits 101 when stdout is a closed pipe. 'atip --help | true', 'atip check ... --json | true' and a failed-level text run all exit 101 (println! panics on EPIPE, outside the catch_unwind in app::main), while 'canon --version | true' exits 141 (default SIGPIPE restored). The brief says atip's exit codes are 0, 1 and 2 only and the checker follows L0 itself (spec 8.4 restores SIGPIPE, 8.6 allows no other exit); atip check run on atip does not see it because the self-check never closes the pipe. Fix: restore the default SIGPIPE disposition at start (as canon does), plus a test that closes the reader before the write.
